what_it_does: Virtual reality (VR) headsets must render (draw) every frame at very high resolution and very low latency — any delay causes nausea. Rendering a full high-resolution image for each eye 90 or more times per second demands enormous compute power. Foveated rendering exploits the fact that the human eye has sharp vision only in a small central area (the fovea) and blurry vision in the periphery: if the system knows exactly where the user's eye is pointing, it can render only that central zone at full quality and use much cheaper, lower-quality rendering for the surrounding area. This paper proposes POLONet, a neural network designed to track eye movement in real time with very low compute cost, and a companion hardware accelerator called POLO, designed to plug into the system-on-chip (SoC — the single integrated chip) inside a VR headset. The hardware-algorithm design is tightly co-optimized so that eye tracking and foveated rendering together consume far less power than either a naive software approach or a generic accelerator.
